question: Charging a cobalt-oxide phone battery to 4.2 volts draws lithium out of the positive electrode. How much of it?
answer: About half. Pull out more and the layered crystal of cobalt oxide becomes unstable: it distorts and can release oxygen, which feeds fires. So a full cell leaves half its lithium where it is. Newer phone cells, charged to about 4.4 volts, reach nearer two-thirds, at some cost in lifespan.
move: Full usually means as far as is safe, not as far as possible.
trap: Nearly all of it, since the battery reads 100%.
reference: Manthiram, A reflection on lithium-ion battery cathode chemistry, Nature Communications, 2020
